issue_context.title: Make a note of the algorithmic complexity of each of the query operations
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

This question comes up pretty regularly. I would like to see this described for:

- archetypal filters: O(a)
- change detection filters: O(a + n)
- ordinary iteration: O(n)
- iter_combinations: ???
- get and get_mut: O(1)
- get_multiple: O(k)
- get_multiple_mut: O(k^2)
comments: I would like to take this. I'm currently working on improving `Query` and `WorldQuery` docs, and I think this data fits very well into a table under a “Performance” section at the bottom of `Query` docs.
Adding one more to that: single and get_single is `O(a)`

review_comments:
I have been trying to figure out whether using a Changed<> filter decreases complexity to the number of changed matching components instead of all (even unchanged) matching components, and this notion of a archetype is new to me. What does this mean exactly, will adding a Changed filter speed up queries or not?

Looking at #5097 seems to indicate that it does not and then this line is maybe worded slightly wrongly. Maybe it should be `a is the number of components in matching archetypes.` as in the mentioned issue?

Seeing as this is a docs change, I think my lacking knowledge is maybe a good thing for improving the quality of the docs.

The asymptotic efficiency of Changed filters is (currently) the same as it performs a binary check for each entity. The performance improvements are if the binary check is faster than the operation you would otherwise do.
